deities: Lord Shiva (also enshrined in the sanctum)

history.period: Modern — construction begun 1974, opened to devotees 1982 (per jharkhand.me). One secondary source (velpu.com) claims 15th-century origin; unverified and in direct conflict with the 1970s account.
history.summary: The Shakti Mandir on Joraphatak Road is one of Dhanbad's most prominent temples, dedicated to Goddess Durga. Local residents founded it in the 1970s (construction 1974, doors opened 1982) to create a dedicated Durga shrine in the city centre. Its signature feature is the Akhand Jyoti (eternal flame) said to have been brought from Vaishno Devi (Jharkhand Tourism says from Vaishno Devi; some sources say Himachal Pradesh). The temple is a white-marble structure whose main sanctum, on the first floor, also houses an image of Lord Shiva — noted by one source as unusual for Jharkhand, where linga worship dominates. Dating conflict flagged above: the 15th-century claim appears in only one secondary source and should not be relied upon.

name: Shakti Mandir
town_description: Dhanbad, in northern Jharkhand, is known as the 'Coal Capital of India' for the Jharia coalfields that drive its economy. It is a major industrial city and one of the region's most important railway junctions.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi (~143 km, per official Jharkhand Tourism)
travel.road: City-centre location on Joraphatak Road; easily reached by auto/taxi from anywhere in Dhanbad

visitor_information.best_time: September to February (winter); Navratri and Diwali for festivals
visitor_information.opening_hours: Aarti times per jharkhand.me: Mangala 5:30 AM, Chhaka 7:00 AM, Bhog 12:00 PM, Sandhya 7:00 PM; one listing shows Sun 9 AM–5 PM / Thu 5 AM–8 PM — verify on visit
